title: Lactic acid bacteria-derived gamma-linolenic acid metabolites are PPARdelta ligands that reduce lipid accumulation in human intestinal organoids.
authors: Noguchi, Makoto; Shimizu, Makoto; Lu, Peng; Takahashi, Yu; Yamauchi, Yoshio; Sato, Shintaro; Kiyono, Hiroshi; Kishino, Shigenobu; Ogawa, Jun; Nagata, Koji; Sato, Ryuichiro
one_liner_zh: 该文研究乳酸菌代谢物作为PPARdelta核受体配体，通过对接模拟分析配体-蛋白结合，但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白-DNA互作，方法仅含简单对接，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: Gut microbiota regulate physiological functions in various hosts, such as energy metabolism and immunity. Lactic acid bacteria, including Lactobacillus plantarum, have a specific polyunsaturated fatty acid saturation metabolism that generates multiple fatty acid species, such as hydroxy fatty acids, oxo fatty acids, conjugated fatty acids, and trans-fatty acids. How these bacterial metabolites impact host physiology is not fully understood. Here, we investigated the ligand activity of lactic acid bacteria-produced fatty acids in relation to nuclear hormone receptors expressed in the small intestine. Our reporter assays revealed two bacterial metabolites of gamma-linolenic acid (GLA), 13-hydroxy-cis-6,cis-9-octadecadienoic acid (gammaHYD), and 13-oxo-cis-6,cis-9-octadecadienoic acid (gammaKetoD) activated peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPARdelta) more potently than GLA. We demonstrate that both gammaHYD and gammaKetoD bound directly to the ligand-binding domain of human PPARdelta. A docking simulation indicated that four polar residues (T289, H323, H449, and Y473) of PPARdelta donate hydrogen bonds to these fatty acids. Interestingly, T289 does not donate a hydrogen bond to GLA, suggesting that bacterial modification of GLA introducing hydroxy and oxo group determines ligand selectivity. In human intestinal organoids, we determined gammaHYD and gammaKetoD increased the expression of PPARdelta target genes, enhanced fatty acid beta-oxidation, and reduced intracellular triglyceride accumulation. These findings suggest that gammaHYD and gammaKetoD, which gut lactic acid bacteria could generate, are naturally occurring PPARdelta ligands in the intestinal tract and may improve lipid metabolism in the human intestine.
abstract_zh: 肠道微生物群调节多种宿主的生理功能，如能量代谢和免疫。乳酸菌，包括植物乳杆菌，具有特定的多不饱和脂肪酸饱和代谢，产生多种脂肪酸种类，如羟基脂肪酸、氧代脂肪酸、共轭脂肪酸和反式脂肪酸。这些细菌代谢物如何影响宿主生理尚未完全明了。在此，我们研究了乳酸菌产生的脂肪酸与小肠中表达的核激素受体的配体活性。我们的报告基因实验揭示，γ-亚麻酸（GLA）的两种细菌代谢物，13-羟基-顺式-6,顺式-9-十八碳二烯酸（gammaHYD）和13-氧代-顺式-6,顺式-9-十八碳二烯酸（gammaKetoD），激活过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体δ（PPARdelta）的效力强于GLA。我们证明gammaHYD和gammaKetoD均直接结合人PPARdelta的配体结合域。对接模拟表明，PPARdelta的四个极性残基（T289、H323、H449和Y473）向这些脂肪酸提供氢键。有趣的是，T289不向GLA提供氢键，这表明GLA的细菌修饰引入羟基和氧代基团决定了配体选择性。在人肠道类器官中，我们确定gammaHYD和gammaKetoD增加了PPARdelta靶基因的表达，增强了脂肪酸β-氧化，并减少了细胞内甘油三酯积累。这些发现表明，肠道乳酸菌可能产生的gammaHYD和gammaKetoD是肠道中天然存在的PPARdelta配体，可能改善人肠道的脂质代谢。
